title: Human Health and Disease
seo_title: Human Health and Disease Class 12 Biology Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 7)
standard_code: Class 12 Biology, Chapter 7: Human Health and Disease
standard_text: Pathogens; parasites causing human diseases (malaria, dengue, chikungunya, filariasis, ascariasis, typhoid, pneumonia, common cold, amoebiasis, ring worm) and their control; basic concepts of immunology – vaccines; cancer, HIV and AIDS; adolescence – drug and alcohol abuse.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 7 Human Health and Disease: common diseases and their pathogens, malaria, immunity and antibodies, vaccines, AIDS, cancer, and drug and alcohol abuse. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Each disease has its own pathogen and way of spreading.
key_sub: Active immunity: own antibodies; passive: ready-made antibodies.
body_html:
How to think about it

Infectious diseases are caused by bacteria (typhoid, pneumonia), viruses (common cold, dengue, AIDS), protozoans (malaria, amoebiasis), worms (ascariasis, filariasis) and fungi (ringworm). Malaria is spread by the female Anopheles mosquito, and Plasmodium multiplies in the liver and red blood cells.

The body defends itself with innate immunity and acquired immunity; B-lymphocytes make antibodies and T-lymphocytes give cell-mediated immunity. Vaccines give active immunity. HIV destroys helper T cells, causing AIDS. Cancer is uncontrolled cell division. Drugs and alcohol harm health and cause dependence, so adolescents should avoid them and seek help.

Example

Typhoid is caused by?

a bacterium

Answer: Salmonella typhi

Example

Antibodies from mother's milk?

ready-made

Answer: passive immunity

Common mistakes

  • Calling malaria a viral disease.
  • Saying vaccines give passive immunity.
  • Thinking antibiotics cure the common cold.

faq.q: What is the difference between active and passive immunity?
faq.a: In active immunity the body makes its own antibodies after infection or vaccination; in passive immunity ready-made antibodies are given.
It infects and destroys helper T-lymphocytes, so the immune system weakens and other infections take hold.
